title: Jazz at Noon in New York three years earlier
summary: His only New York date in years was a Jazz at Noon Friday session for Les Leiber with amateur businessmen players.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: O.K. Nick I want to talk now a little bit about these past few months when you've

come back into New York, though you're still living in Charlottesville, still based there, you've come back up now three times. When was the last time you had a date in New York before this one in September of '79?
Well, I did the jazz at noon about three years ago for Les Leiber.
That's while you were living in Charlottesville, that you came up?
Yeah, I did that for him. That was very nice and that was the only thing I've done in the last six or seven years in New York, or eight years. Yeah.
How did that particular thing come about?
Well, I knew about it and so I came up here on a holiday. So he said, you know, it's a thing that everybody does, you know, Billy Taylor Jr., and Clark Terry and all

the guys do. Milt Hinton and all the guys do it. It's just one of those things, you know, and it's these business men that played music, that played jazz to help their way through college or whatever or they played it in their youth. And on Friday afternoon, instead of going back to work, they come up to Jazz at Noon and they play and they have a guest, you know, every Sunday. Of course Les plays alto himself, you know, and he plays too and it's a nice atmosphere, you know.
So that was just one Sunday (Friday) about three years ago?
